where: ?range=today|7d|30d, Owner, EN and TR. 11 days since Oct 1 are unclosed; one guest in house every night.
observed: Headline occupancy covers closed days only; the table beneath includes open days. Today tab: 0.0%, "0 / 0 Occupied Nights", table row 33.3%. Last 7 days: 0.0%, "0 / 0", seven rows of 33.3%. Last 30 days: 11.1% (2 / 18) above a table with 13 occupied nights. The Today page says Occupancy 33%, in house 1 / 3. None of these views says "closed days only".
expected: The Today tab to say 33% like the Today page and like its own row. If a figure excludes open days, the page must say so, as the month view does ("closed days only, N of M").
suggested_fix: Occupancy does not need a charge: count open days in occupancy (the month table already shows 33.3% for them). Keep ADR/RevPAR closed-days-only and say so with the same badge the month view uses. Better: retire the old component and make the windows a month-view variant.

where: Month Sep 2026 and all trailing windows, Owner/Manager/Front Desk. 2 occupied nights, both "No price on the booking".
observed: Unknown shown as zero. Month view: RevPAR "TRY 0.00 room revenue ÷ 18 available nights" and Room revenue "TRY 0.00" while 2 of 2 occupied nights have no price. ADR is correctly "—". Trailing windows: ADR is "TRY 0.00" (month view says "—" for the same data). Total revenue "TRY 0.00", Payments "TRY 0.00".
expected: An unpriced night is not a night that earned zero. RevPAR and revenue should carry a warning next to the number ("2 occupied nights have no price; revenue is understated"), and ADR should be "—" in every view.
suggested_fix: When uncharged nights > 0, put one line under RevPAR, Net room revenue and Total revenue linking to the "Nights with no charge" section. Make the trailing windows use the same dash rule.

where: ?month=2026-09 (a finished month), all four roles. 6 of 30 days closed.
observed: September is labelled "Month to date · 6 of 30 days closed" and says "Today is still open: its nights are not charged until the day closes". It is a past month. 24 of 30 rows say "Open day · Not yet charged", including Sep 1 to 20 when the Property had no units (available = 0) and Sep 21 to 24, which the Close day screen does not list as waiting (it starts at Oct 1) and does not list as closed (its history starts Sep 25).
expected: A finished month with unclosed days should say "Incomplete: 24 of 30 days were never closed" and name the reason. Days before the Property had any unit should read "Before opening", not "Open day". The "Today" sentence is wrong for any month but the current one.
suggested_fix: Derive the badge from whether the month has ended, not from "any day not closed" (cause: server/analytics.ts sets state "open" whenever closedDays.length !== monthDays.length). Add a state for "ended, incomplete". Mark pre-opening days.
basis: Label and rows verified; cause inferred from code. Reproduced Y (4 roles)

where: Default landing /en/analytics = October 2026, Owner. 0 of 31 days closed, 10 days waiting on Close day.
observed: The first thing the owner sees is three dashes and a column of TRY 0.00. The note blames only today ("Today is still open"), but 11 days are open, 10 of them waiting for someone to close them. The page never says that, and never links to Close day.
expected: "10 days are waiting to be closed, so October has no figures yet" with a link to Close day for roles that may close. For other roles, name who closes the day.
suggested_fix: Read the waiting-days count (Close day already computes it) and show it in the badge area with a link.

observed: The comparison line reads "There is no earlier month to compare with." on October, where September exists and has data (the comparison covers the same elapsed days = 0, so no figures). It is also shown for September, where August is empty (correct there). The same sentence covers two different situations. The month "previous" arrow in September is enabled although the line says there is none.
expected: "No closed days yet, so there is nothing to compare" for October; "August had no activity" for September.
suggested_fix: Split the message by cause (the code already knows: elapsed = 0 versus prior without figures).
basis: Text verified; cause inferred from buildMonthReport

observed: Open days show "33.3%" occupancy in every row (Oct 1 to 11) while the headline is "—", the total row is "—" and the page says open days "count toward no rate". Rows and total disagree on the same screen. The one-guest-in-every-night pattern comes from an overdue departure (Today: "Was due to leave on Oct 1"), which nothing on Analytics hints at.
expected: Either show open-day occupancy in the headline (see 01) or show "—" in rows and say why.
suggested_fix: Decide one rule for occupancy on open days and apply it to headline, total row and rows.

where: Front Desk (frontdesk@), Manager, Finance (Finance is expected to), month and all windows.
observed: Front Desk sees every money figure: net/total revenue, ADR, RevPAR, revenue booked, money collected, collected by method. The gate is finance.manage_folio; the shipped Front Desk role holds it because check-in opens a folio (migration 20260916002300 comment). The permission that lets a clerk open a folio also lets them read the hotel's monthly takings.
expected: Whether the clerk should read property revenue is an owner decision. The screen's own docs call this "governed financial visibility", but the gate does not govern it from the front desk.
suggested_fix: Decision, not a defect to fix quietly: either accept it and say so in the feature doc, or add a separate "view revenue reports" permission and grant it to Owner/Manager/Finance only.
basis: Visible verified; intent inferred from migration

observed: The hidden money is explained, but in system words: "You do not hold permission to view financial metrics (finance.manage_folio)." It shows a raw permission key and does not say who to ask. The month note above it still says "Every rate and revenue figure covers the closed days only" to a reader who sees none.
expected: "Revenue figures are visible to Owner, Manager, Finance and Front Desk. Ask your manager if you need them." No key.
suggested_fix: Replace the string; drop the revenue sentence for masked readers.

observed: Two designs behind one tab bar. Trailing windows: title "Analytics & Reporting" under "Analytics", columns "Occupied Units / Available Units" holding night counts, card "3 Sellable Units", "Total Revenue" captioned "Total Revenue", no arithmetic under any figure, English-only phrasing like "RevPAR (Revenue Per Available Room)" while the month view says "per available night". Switching tab changes layout, vocabulary and rules (closed-only versus not).
expected: One screen, one vocabulary, one rule. The month view's arithmetic lines are what a non-accountant needs and the windows lack them.
suggested_fix: Rebuild the windows on the month components (see 01). At minimum align labels (nights, not units) and add the division under each figure.

where: ?range=30d, Owner. Sep 12 to 20: the Property had no units.
observed: Nine rows show "0 Occupied, 0 Available, 0.0%" with an empty bar. The month view correctly shows "—" for those same days. The feature's own rule (AN-S2-03) says nothing happening is not zero percent.
expected: "—" when available nights = 0.
suggested_fix: One-line fix in the old table.

where: Day drill-down ?day=2026-09-30 and "Nights with no charge", Owner.
observed: The drawer shows stay 102 with "No price on the booking", but nothing to open: no link to the reservation or folio, and "Nights with no charge" has no action either. The owner learns a booking has no price and must find it elsewhere.
expected: A link from the stay to its reservation (role-aware) so the price can be fixed.
suggested_fix: Add a link in the stay row; reservation screen already exists.
basis: Missing link verified; whether the reservation can still be priced unknown

observed: Only the two-character date cell ("27 Sun") is a link; the row has no hover or arrow, so nothing says a day opens. The link's aria-label is "Show Sunday, Sep 27, 2026", which replaces the visible text "27 Sun". 30 small targets on a phone.
expected: Whole row is the target, or a visible "Details" cue.
suggested_fix: Make the row a link or add a chevron; make the accessible name contain the visible text.
basis: Link scope verified; WCAG label-in-name inferred

where: EN versus TR versus AR, month view.
observed: Currency is written three ways: EN "TRY 0.00", TR "₺0,00", AR "0.00 TRY" with Latin digits. TR is the only one using the lira sign. The Arabic percent carries direction marks ("11.1‎%‎"), harmless on screen.
expected: One currency convention per locale, chosen on purpose.
suggested_fix: Check formatMinorMoney currency display option for EN.
basis: verified; whether EN "TRY" is deliberate unknown

observed: No horizontal overflow and the tables restack with labels (good), but the page is about 9,600 px tall: three full-width headline cards, then 30 day cards. The first screen is two paragraphs of caveat plus one card; ADR is below the fold, so occupancy, ADR and RevPAR cannot be read together on a phone. The sticky bottom bar covers the lower card edge.
expected: A manager checking occupancy on a phone sees all three headline figures without scrolling past the notes.
suggested_fix: Put the three figures in a compact row above the notes, or collapse the day table behind a toggle.
basis: verified at 375 px emulation, one run

observed: The sidebar stays open from 768 px up and takes about 40% of the width. The table scrolls sideways inside its own box (scroller 923 px wide in a 464 px box at 768). The Check in button measured at x=1050 to 1134 on a 1024 px and on a 768 px screen, i.e. off screen. Readiness and Balance are cut too. At 375 px the row shows Guest, Reservation and half of Room; there is no hint that more is to the right. At 1180 px it fits (Check in right edge 1166 px, measured in the Turkish page).
expected: The one button I press 30 times a day visible at every width a desk tablet uses (iPad landscape is 1024).
suggested_fix: Collapse the sidebar by default below about 1280 px, and/or pin the action column to the right edge, and/or show each row as a card below 1024 px (guest, room, readiness, button).

observed: No default sort is set in the table (useState([])), so rows come in the query's order: room name, then Unit, then guest (listArrivals in the reservations module). The expected time is printed inside the Reservation column, whose sort key is the reference code, so the time cannot be sorted. Checked-in rows are mixed in with the ones still to come. Late arrivals (shown by "N days late") are not grouped.
expected: The next arrival first, overdue ones highlighted at the top, checked-in ones last or folded away. The Departures screen already puts "who has already left" under "who is still to go".
suggested_fix: Default order: overdue, then by expected time (none last), then by room. Make Expected its own sortable column. Group or fold "Checked in".
evidence: 01-arrivals-desktop.png shows only one row, so the order itself was not seen. Reproduced N.
basis: inferred (code); the unsortable time is also visible in the column headers

where: Front Desk, any row with no expected time.
observed: The row says "Expected —" (a dash). "No expected time" exists only for screen readers. A dash after "Expected" reads as "not loaded". Turkish shows "Beklenen —".
expected: "No time given" in muted text, or nothing.
suggested_fix: Show the words, or hide the line when there is no time.

where: Front Desk, a "Not ready" room (the only data state present).
observed: The badge says only "Not ready". The cause (dirty, or waiting for inspection) is known to the system but not shown; the warning text that appears after pressing Check in says "it hasn't been cleaned, or it's waiting for inspection", an either/or. The row menu offers only "Show on the room map": no link to Housekeeping, no way to see who is cleaning it or when it will be done. To learn anything more I must press Check in, get the question, then press "Check in anyway": two presses and a server round trip. I did not press it (audit rule); the flow is read from check-in-action.tsx and the module, where the "not ready" answer rolls back the Stay.
expected: The badge names the cause. The question names the room and offers a way to ask Housekeeping or open its status, beside "Check in anyway".
suggested_fix: Put the cause in the badge ("Dirty", "Awaiting inspection"). In the question use the room name and the cause. Add "Open in Housekeeping" to the row menu.
evidence: 01-arrivals-desktop.png, 02-row-menu.png. Badge and menu reproduced Y; the question is stopped before submit, not persisted.

where: Front Desk. A guest who arrives a day early, or one booked for tomorrow.
observed: The list holds only today's bookings and late ones. Searching for an early guest gives "Nothing matches these filters." with no pointer to Reservations. The desk must leave, find the booking in Reservations, use Change booking to start today, then come back. Docs: CI-S1-21 is still open (recommends a muted "arriving next business day" group with a "Change to start today" action); CI-DEF-01 is deferred and its text is out of date, because Change booking now exists.
expected: Search that falls back to "also look at upcoming bookings", or a muted group below today's list.
suggested_fix: When search finds nothing, add a link "Search all reservations for this" carrying the text. Then build CI-S1-21.
evidence: 05-search-no-match.png. The empty search reproduced Y; the early-guest path is inferred.

where: Front Desk. A walk-in with no booking.
observed: Arrivals has no "New booking" action. A walk-in is booked in Reservations and then checked in, as CI-S1-08 says; from this page there is no hint of that route.
expected: A "Walk-in" button on the page header that opens the booking form for today and returns to this list.
suggested_fix: Add the entry point. The booking form already exists in Reservations (new-reservation-dialog.tsx).

where: Front Desk, keyboard only, a queue.
observed: From the "Skip to content" link, Check in on the first row is 9 Tab presses away (search, Columns, 5 sort headers, Copy reference, Check in); every further row adds 3 stops (copy, check in, menu). After a successful check-in the Check in button is replaced by Undo, and focus is only restored for the undo path (check-in-focus.ts), so focus falls back to the page. The user then re-tabs from the top for every guest. The check-in button's accessible name is just "Check in" on every row (only the menu button carries the guest's name).
expected: After a check-in focus moves to the next row's Check in; each button names its guest ("Check in mahnoor") and the Copy button is not in the way.
suggested_fix: Claim focus after "done" for the next actionable row; add an accessible name with the guest; take Copy reference out of the tab order (or put it after the action).
evidence: Tab count verified from the page's focusable elements; focus loss inferred from code. Reproduced Y (count), N (focus loss).

observed: The browser tab is titled "Ranza" on Arrivals and on every other screen. A desk that keeps Arrivals and Departures open in two windows (the page's own code comment describes this) cannot tell the tabs apart.
expected: "Arrivals · Demo Otel İstanbul" in the tab.
suggested_fix: Set the page metadata title per route.
evidence: Seen in the browser's page list for my tab. Reproduced Y.

where: Front Desk, a shift-long open tab.
observed: The list polls every 30 s and pauses when the tab is hidden, but nothing on screen says how fresh it is. A refused poll leaves the last good rows and their Check in buttons on screen (the docs record this as CI-DIFF-01, "current behaviour differs"). A signed-out desk keeps showing guests' names and a button that will be refused.
expected: "Updated 14:02" next to the title and a visible "can't refresh" warning with a Refresh button.
suggested_fix: Show last-updated time; on a 401 or failure show a banner and disable Check in.
evidence: No such indicator in any screenshot (01). Reproduced N for the failure case.

where: Front Desk, a check-in that fails.
observed: Several different causes (stale row, permission, closed day, lost connection, an unexpected error) all end as "That Reservation cannot be checked in." No next step. The unexpected-error case is logged by the server to the console only (console.error), not to Observatory. Double-press is safe: the button is disabled while the request runs and the database lock gives one Stay and one refusal (CI-S1-11).
expected: Tell the desk whether to retry, reload or ask a manager.
suggested_fix: Split "refused" into "reload the list" (stale) and "ask a manager" (permission), and send unexpected failures to the shared error reporter.
evidence: Not triggered (would require a submit). Reproduced N.

observed: The column says "Room and bed" and the Turkish and Arabic use room words, but the dialogs say "Unit" ("Unit 201", "another Unit", "Suite has no price"). One page, two words for the same thing. The Change booking dialog also says "Keep as it was" while the no-show dialog says "Keep the booking".
expected: One term (Room) and one wording for the cancel button.
suggested_fix: Replace "Unit" in dialogs shown to desk staff; align the cancel labels.

observed: The Balance column shows "No Folio" for every arrival, because the Folio is opened at check-in. It uses a column of width for a constant, and "Folio" is back-office language. The second line of the Guest cell reads "Guest, until Oct 12, 2026": the word "Guest" is the stay type and adds nothing; the number of nights and the room type's price are not shown.
expected: Nights ("1 night"), and the balance column hidden until it has a value.
suggested_fix: Show "1 night, until Oct 12". Hide the Balance column while no row has a Folio, or show "Due at check-in" once deposits exist.

observed: The search placeholder is cut off: "Search Guest / Room and bed / Reserva".
expected: A placeholder that fits.
suggested_fix: "Search guest, room or reference".

observed: Both see the full list read-only. Housekeeping's row menu has one item ("Show on the room map"); there is no link to mark the room clean, which is the one thing the role comes for. Finance sees no actions and a "No Folio" balance, with no note that the role cannot check in (the action cell is simply empty). This matches FD-S5-03 and FD-S7-05: the controls are hidden by design.
expected: For Housekeeping: a link to the room in Housekeeping. For read-only roles: a muted "View only".
suggested_fix: Add the Housekeeping link; show a "View only" hint in the action cell.

where: Front Desk, a busy day (more than 10 arrivals).
observed: The table shows 10 rows per page. Sort, search and page size are held in component state, so they reset on a reload and on every visit. On a 40-arrival day that is four pages, in room order.
expected: All of today's arrivals on one scrollable page, or a remembered page size.
suggested_fix: Default the page size to 50 for this screen, or remember it.
evidence: Page-size selector shows 10 (01). Behaviour on 40 rows not seen.

observed: "Mark as no-show" is two clicks from the list and cannot be taken back (the dialog says so, which is good). It is offered from the first minute of the arrival day, with no hint of the expected time having passed, and sits directly under "Change booking" in the same menu.
expected: A warning when the expected time has not passed, or no-show offered after the expected time or a cut-off.
suggested_fix: Show the expected-time status in the dialog. Rule FD-S4-04 allows it on the day, so this is a policy choice, not a bug.

observed: The details table shows raw field names (changeId, toEndsOn, fromEndsOn) and the word "None" for "no departure before". A "Role changed" record on the same screen reads "From Finance / To Housekeeping". A reservation record shows "Amount: None". A "Details" caption is also rendered as visible text under the table.
expected: Every action reads like the role change: "Departure: none, then 1 Oct 2026". No internal field names.
suggested_fix: Add the stay and reservation change keys to the context vocabulary in context-facts.tsx; render a missing value as "not set"; hide the table caption. The code deliberately prints unknown keys as themselves (words.ts comment), so this will recur for each new writer unless a test fails on an unlabelled key.

observed: An event names its subject ("Reservation · guest · room", "Stay · guest · room") as plain text. Only a Folio subject is a link (to Finance). I cannot jump from "Departure changed" to the booking, the stay or the room.
expected: The subject is a link to its page (reservation, stay, room, staff member) wherever such a page exists.
suggested_fix: Link reservation, stay and unit subjects the way the Folio is linked in record-panel.tsx; keep the Property in the URL.
evidence: 02 · reproduced Y · verified (record screen), inferred (code: only subjectType === "folio" links)

where: Finance / reservation screens → Audit log · Owner
observed: "Why does this balance differ?" starts on a Folio, but I found no link from a Folio or reservation to its own history; the log links to the Folio, not the other way. Searching the Guest's name in the log is the only route.
expected: A "History" link on a Folio or reservation that opens the log narrowed to it.
suggested_fix: Support ?subject= in the log filters and add the link where the owner already looks. Today's activity card does link into the log (code), so the pattern exists.
evidence: grep of features/finance and features/reservations found no audit-log reference · inferred

observed: Typing "rate" into Search returns "Nothing matches these filters. Widen the dates, choose another action, or clear the filters." Search covers Guest, room, colleague and reason text only, so a person who thinks in the words on screen finds nothing, and the empty state does not say search ignores action names. The Action select has 56 entries in one flat, unsorted-by-topic list (it is searchable).
expected: Typing the words in an action name ("rate", "cancelled", "check-in") finds those events, or the empty state says "search does not look at action names, use the Action filter".
suggested_fix: Match the search text against the localized action labels on the server, or suggest the Action filter in the empty state. Group the 56 actions by area (Reservations, Money, Staff, Rooms, Maintenance, HR).

where: List · Owner · desktop 1440 and wider · record with a long reason
observed: The "Why" text runs off the right edge of the table and is cut mid-word ("...meets RG-S1"). The code intends a two-line clamp, but the column never wraps. In Arabic the same text is cut on the left. The full reason is only on the record screen.
expected: The reason wraps to two lines with an ellipsis, so the first words of why are always readable.
suggested_fix: Give the Why cell a fixed max width so line-clamp-2 applies; keep the record screen as the full view.

observed: The five filters stack to about one full screen before the first record. The table is 1263 px wide inside a 341 px frame, so only When and What are visible; Who and Why sit off screen with no cue to scroll. The owner on a phone sees what happened but not who did it.
expected: On a phone each event is a card: when, what, who, why. Filters collapse behind one "Filter" button.
suggested_fix: Render rows as stacked cards under a breakpoint; collapse the filter form. The page has no horizontal page scroll (document width = 375), only the inner table.
evidence: 11, 15 · reproduced Y · verified. The same happens at 768 px: the table is 1276 px wide in a 462 px frame beside the sidebar, so only When and What show and the Where column is cut at the edge (screenshot 15, in Turkish).

where: List · Owner · search of one character
observed: Typing "a" shows a small grey line "Type at least two characters to search" but the full, unfiltered list and "15 records" stay below, next to a search box that reads "a". It looks like a result.
expected: Hide the table or dim it until the search is valid, or put the message at the search box.
suggested_fix: Render the message inside the Search field and skip the table.
evidence: 07 · reproduced Y · verified. This matches the written rule AL-S1-24, so it is polish, not a defect against the spec.

where: Action names and subject labels vs sibling screens · Owner
observed: One log mixes "Reservation taken" with "Booking cancelled" and "Booking changed"; shows "Accommodation unit" as the type of a room where the rest of the product says Room; "Business day closed" where the Close the day screen says "Close the day"; "Unit added" / "Unit blocked" beside "Room status changed"; "Nightly rates changed" for a price list.
expected: One word per thing across the product.
suggested_fix: Pick Reservation or Booking, Room or Unit, and align auditAction and auditSubject in messages.ts (all three languages) with the sibling screens.

observed: Seven rows in a row read "Room check after cleaning changed · Property · (the Property's name)" at the same minute. The list does not show the before/after value, so the owner must open each one to learn it was Off then On. Under pressure, "who changed this rate" means opening every "Nightly rates changed" row in turn.
expected: A one-setting change shows "Off → On" (or "₺1.500 → ₺1.750") on the list row.
suggested_fix: Let ContextFacts expose a one-line summary for single-setting and price changes and use it as the second line in the What cell.
evidence: 01, 04 · reproduced Y · verified. The rate-change record itself is inferred (code and edge-cases.csv); none exists on staging.

observed: Times are the Property's wall clock (verified: "Sep 29, 2026, 13:08" style, 24-hour), but nothing on the row says which clock; the sentence explaining it sits under the table, after up to 50 rows. A record about the whole Organization uses the opened Property's clock.
expected: The When header or filter bar says "Times in Istanbul (UTC+3)".
suggested_fix: Put the zone name in the When column header.

where: List · Owner · search in a large hotel
observed: The search resolves a text to at most 200 Guests, 200 rooms and 200 colleagues (MATCH_LIMIT), then looks for events about them. A two-letter fragment that matches more than 200 Guests silently drops the rest, and the screen then says "N records" as if complete. "Nothing happened" and "my search was too broad" look the same.
expected: "More than 200 matches, type more of the name" when the cap is hit.
suggested_fix: Have searchIds return whether it hit the cap and show a line; or raise the minimum length.
evidence: Code packages/ranza/core/src/audit-log.ts lines 82-89 · inferred; staging has too few Guests to trigger it.

observed: The log offers no export or pointer to one. The Data export screen has an "Audit log" dataset gated by audit.read and sits one row above Audit log in the rail, but the log never says so. An owner collecting evidence for an accountant or an insurer will look for a download button here.
expected: A "Download these records" link that opens Data export with this dataset selected.
suggested_fix: Link to /data-export with the dataset preselected; filters are not carried today (unknown whether the export supports them).
evidence: Rail screenshot 01; messages.ts dataset label and migration 20260916010700 · inferred (I did not open the Data export screen)

observed: Audit log is the last item, under Data export. use-case.mmd records "where it sits in the rail" as an open question. In the urgent case the owner has to scroll a 15-item rail; at 375 px the bottom bar shows about five destinations at a time.
expected: One obvious route in under a minute.
suggested_fix: Keep it last (it is consulted, not worked) but make sure a second entry exists: Today's activity card links to the log for audit.read holders (code), and AUDIT-03 would add one from Folios. Close the open question in the diagram.

observed: Heading says "Thursday, October 1, 2026 is ready to close" and a badge says "10 days waiting". Only Oct 1 can be closed. The automatic close stopped after Sep 30 because 102 is still in house. The same Guest stays open on every later day, so each of the ten closes asks for a reason, and the dialog is re-keyed per day so a reason is not carried over.
expected: To see the range (Oct 1 to Oct 10), which days have blockers, and clear them once.
suggested_fix: Show the range and the per-day open counts. When the same item is open on several days, offer one close of all of them with one reason. At minimum, say "the same Guest holds all 10 days".
basis: verified for the 10-day count and the single offered day; inferred that ten reasons will be needed (edge-cases CD-S1-07, CD-S1-22; key={day.dayToClose} in close-day-view.tsx). I did not close any day.

where: /en/close-day, Manager and Front Desk, overdue departure
observed: On the overdue row "ahmed, 102, Due out Oct 1, 2026" the filled primary button is Extend; Open departures is the quiet one. The Extend dialog says "A Guest's extra nights are charged at the booking's own price", but the Room nights card on the same page says this booking has "No price on the booking". Extending to clear the blocker would also record a Guest as in house who may have left ten days ago.
expected: For a Guest ten days overdue, Check out as the main action; Extend only when the Guest is really staying, with a warning when the booking has no price.
suggested_fix: Make Open departures primary on overdue rows, show "10 days overdue", and add the no-price warning to the Extend dialog.

observed: The dialog says "1 item is still open. It is recorded with the close, with your reason." It does not say which item. The sentence about what the close charges ("charges the night of every Guest whose booking has a price") exists only in the no-items variant, so with items open the one consequence that touches money is not stated. It does say reopening is not available yet.
expected: Name the open items, and always say what will be charged and what will not (here: 0 nights charged, 1 not charged, and who).
suggested_fix: List the open items by name in the dialog. Show the room-night line in both variants.
basis: verified for the open-items variant; inferred for the no-items variant (dialogQuiet text in messages.ts at HEAD).

observed: The row says "102 · Due out Oct 1, 2026". It does not say how late (10 days) and, unlike the arrivals rows, shows no reservation reference. After Open departures and a check-out, the page's Back button goes one level up (Today), not back to Close the day, so the next blocker means going through the rail.
expected: "10 days overdue", the reference, and a way back to the close.
suggested_fix: Add days overdue and the reference to the row. Return to Close the day after a check-out started from it.
basis: verified for the missing age and reference, and that Back on Close the day points to Today; inferred that Back on Departures does the same (ADR 0035).

observed: "No price on the booking · 1: ahmed · 102" is listed, with no link to the booking or to anywhere a price can be set. Recent closes already show "1 not charged" on Sep 29 and Sep 30 and will show it for each of the ten days waiting. where: Owner, Nightly rates card, Demo Property with 3 units and no prices

where: Owner, Housekeeping card (“Check rooms after cleaning”) and Maintenance card (3 questions × Organization default / This Property)

where: Owner, any card with a draft; also leaving by sidebar link or browser Back

where: Owner, Property card, currency, on a Property whose currency is still changeable (not reachable on staging, it is already locked)

observed: Price fields are offered for Bed and Apartment, which the Property has none of (“None at this Property yet”). Nothing says whether pricing them now has any effect.
expected: Either hidden or labelled “applies when you add one”.
suggested_fix: One line of copy.

expected: One card anatomy for every section.

where: /en/data-export, Front Desk and Housekeeping, typed URL
observed: The page shows "This module is not in your Subscription. It appears here once your Organization subscribes to it and the Property has it enabled." The same Organization shows the module to Owner, Manager and Finance, so the Subscription is not the cause: the Front Desk and Housekeeping roles lack data_export.read. The rail correctly hides the entry for both. Housekeeping showed exactly the same text (read from the page, no separate screenshot).
expected: "You do not have permission to export data. Ask an Owner." A front-desk user told the company has not subscribed will report a billing problem or stop asking.
suggested_fix: In page.tsx the single !property branch covers both "not entitled" and "no permission". Split it: when the Property is entitled but the role lacks the permission, render a permission message.

where: New Export form, Finance and Manager
observed: The form is identical for every role: all five datasets are enabled, Guests and Reservations are pre-ticked. Per the docs, Guests and Reservations need a front-desk permission and the Audit log needs audit.read (EXP-S1-01, EXP-DEF-04 says the guest rule "excludes Finance and Housekeeping"). The refusal happens on submit, with one generic sentence "You may not request an export of these datasets" that does not say which (EXP-S1-46 states this is deliberate). I did not press submit to see it.
expected: The Finance accountant should see only what the role may export, with Folios and Payments ticked, or each blocked dataset disabled with a one-line reason. Pressing the default button should not be a guaranteed refusal.
suggested_fix: Expose the role's allowed datasets to the form (the map exists in app.data_export_resource_permissions()), disable the rest with "needs front desk access", pre-tick the allowed set. Whether Finance holds data_export.create at all is unknown.

where: New Export, any role, default state
observed: The form opens with Guests and Reservations ticked and CSV chosen. When several datasets are chosen in CSV, the code stacks them in one file, each under a # dataset: name line with a blank line between (renderCsv), and a spreadsheet opens it as one sheet. The form does not say this. Someone who wants "my guest list for the new software" and does not untick Reservations gets a file that no importer reads. Documented as deferred (EXP-DEF-02).
expected: Either one file per dataset, or a visible line under the datasets: "Several datasets in CSV are stacked in one file. Choose one dataset per export if you want to import it." Better: pre-tick nothing.
suggested_fix: Short term: pre-tick nothing and add the sentence when two or more datasets and CSV are chosen. Long term: zip of one CSV per dataset (EXP-DEF-02).
effort: S for the warning, L for the zip

where: New Export and Create Schedule, all roles
observed: The page never says what an export contains in scope. Code: it is every row, all dates, everything the requester can read (EXP-S1-23, reach not the Property in the header). The header shows "Demo Otel İstanbul" and the description says "your organization". An owner of two Properties cannot tell whether the file is this hotel or both, and the accountant cannot tell whether it is this year or all time.
expected: A one-line scope statement above the Request button: "All dates. Properties you have access to: A, B." Plus a date range (see Not built).
suggested_fix: Add the scope line first (S). Date range is backend work.
basis: verified absence of text, inferred actual scope

where: Any export that grows past 100,000 rows in one dataset or 25 MiB
observed: The export fails with "Too large to export." and nothing else. With no date range and no way to export one Property or a smaller piece, the owner has no way to make it smaller. The limit is 100,000 rows per dataset and 25 MiB per file (contracts.ts, EXP-S1-45, runner.ts). Folio lines and the audit log of a busy hotel will reach 100,000 rows. Failing loudly rather than truncating is correct; the dead end is the problem. Not seen on screen (empty data).
expected: The failed row says what to do ("Choose fewer datasets or a shorter period") and the form offers a way to narrow.
suggested_fix: Add a next step to the failure text now (S); a date range makes it actionable (M, backend).

observed: The Guests dataset is names, emails, phone numbers; Folio lines carry free-text descriptions; the Audit log carries context. Nothing on the page warns that the file contains personal data, how long it stays available (7 days is shown only on a ready row, never on the form), or who can download it (anyone holding the read permission plus the dataset permissions, EXP-S1-38). The only hint is the card text "Names, email addresses and phone numbers".
expected: A sentence on the form: "This file contains guest personal data. Store it securely. Anyone with export access can download it for 7 days. Requests and downloads are logged." Turkish customers will expect a KVKK note.
suggested_fix: Add the notice to the form and to the ready row.

observed: The five datasets are the only things that can leave: guests, reservations and stays, rooms and beds, folios and payments, audit log (datasets.ts). Staff, HR and payroll, rates, food and beverage, inventory, maintenance requests, housekeeping history and guest-experience requests have no dataset. The page does not say so. For "be sure nothing about the hotel is trapped", the owner is falsely reassured by a list that looks complete. A fifth caveat: after a Subscription ends, every dataset except the audit log returns no data (EXP-DEF-03, owner decision still open).
expected: A short "Not included yet" list under the datasets, or a link to a page saying how to get the rest.
suggested_fix: Add a static note listing what is not included. Whether to build the rest is a product decision (see section 6).

observed: The filename is export- plus the first 8 characters of the id plus the extension (migration 20260916010710, line 550; the link falls back to the same pattern). Twenty exports a quarter means twenty indistinguishable files in the Downloads folder, with nothing to say which hotel, dataset or date.
expected: Something like prizic-demo-guests-2026-10-11.csv.
suggested_fix: Build the name in the database function from Organization, dataset keys and the request date.

observed: The table shows requested time, requester, datasets, format, status, size, action. The record counts per dataset are stored (recordCounts, and a "Records" header string exists in the messages) but the table does not render them. A 1 KB size is the only clue that an export is empty, and an empty dataset keeps its header row (EXP-S1-43), so it looks like a success.
expected: "1,248 guests, 3,102 reservations" on the row, so the owner can check the number against what they know before trusting the file.
suggested_fix: Render recordCounts in the datasets cell or a Records column.

observed: Columns are raw database names: amount_minor (integer minor units, so 5000 means 50.00), reservation_status, stay_type, UUID ids, created_at as an ISO instant (UTC). The Folios card promises "charges, payments, and balances" and the column list has no balance column. No VAT or tax column and no invoice-style layout. An accountant will need to rebuild the file before the tax office can use it.
expected: Headers in plain words in the user's language, money as decimals with the currency, and the card text matching what the file holds.
suggested_fix: Correct the card text now (S). Human-readable headers and decimal amounts are a design decision (M).

where: History table, pending / processing / failed / expired rows
observed: While waiting, the row shows an italic "Pending" or "Processing" with no elapsed time. The worker picks requests up every 15 s and the page re-reads every 5 s (data-export.service.ts, data-export-view.tsx), so a normal wait is about 20 s. If the worker is down, a pending row has no timeout in the UI; the sweep only fails a processing row after 30 minutes (EXP-S1-31). Failed and expired rows end with a reason or a word and no button to request the same thing again. Whether the worker is running on staging is unknown.
expected: "Requested 14 minutes ago, still waiting" in a warning tone after a few minutes, and a "Request again" button on failed and expired rows that reopens the form with the same choices.
suggested_fix: Add elapsed time and "Request again".

where: Schedules tab and Create Schedule form
observed: The form asks for name, frequency (daily, weekly, monthly), format and datasets. It does not ask for a weekday or time of day and does not say when the first run will be (the code sets it one step from now, EXP-S1-34). A paused schedule shows only "Paused", with no reason, even when it was paused because the creator lost permission (EXP-S1-33). There is no edit or delete in the table, only Pause and Resume. The card says "Active Export Schedules" but lists paused ones too. Each run just lands in the history for 7 days; nobody is emailed. The example name "Weekly Financial Backup" (Turkish placeholder) and the JSON hint "backup" suggest a backup, while a monthly schedule's file expires after 7 days unless somebody logs in to fetch it.
expected: Say when it runs and where the result appears, show why a schedule is paused, and be honest that this is not a backup.
suggested_fix: Add the "next run" text and the "appears here for 7 days" line to the form; add a paused reason; rename the card.

The link is a plain <a download>, so the click ends in a browser "failed" download or an empty tab with no message in Ranza.
expected: A readable message: "This file is no longer available. Request it again."
suggested_fix: Return a small JSON or redirect to the page with a toast.

observed: The page scrolls sideways: document width 885 px in a 768 px viewport. The "Create Export Schedule" button is cut off at the right edge ("Create E") and the breadcrumb reads "WORKSP". Measured twice (screenshot, then script). At 375 px there was no horizontal overflow.

suggested_fix: Allow the tab/button row to wrap.

observed: Four large tiles sit above the work: "Recent Export Records 0", "Ready 0", "Active Export Schedules 0", and a tile titled "Requested At" holding "—" (it means the time of the last export). expected: Short labels ("Exports", "Ready", "Schedules", "Last export") and smaller tiles, or none.
suggested_fix: Rename the tiles; drop them on small screens.

where: Header of the page, all roles
observed: "Export History" and "Schedules" are tabs; "New Export" and "Create Export Schedule" are buttons that swap the same panel. When a button is active, no tab is highlighted, so there is no marker for where I am, and the form has no Cancel. After a successful request the page returns to History by itself after one second.
expected: Four views as one navigation, or two forms opened as a panel with a Cancel link.
suggested_fix: Make the four panels one tab set, or add Cancel.

expected: The three names read in order with the Arabic "and" between them.

observed: The tables format times with toLocaleString(locale) in a client component, so the time shown is in the browser's time zone and with the locale's short date, not in the Property's zone (Europe/Istanbul) that the Today page shows. The file itself holds UTC ISO instants. An accountant abroad will see a different time from the audit log.
expected: Property time zone, with an unambiguous date.
suggested_fix: Format on the server with the Property time zone.

observed: The Download button is the last of seven columns inside an overflow-x-auto wrapper, so on a phone the person must scroll sideways to find the one thing the page is for. No row exists on staging to see it.
expected: On narrow screens each export is a card with Download visible.
suggested_fix: Card layout below sm.

where: New Export, format picker, keyboard only

where: /tr/departures?show=owing (the link a figure on Today builds), Front Desk, 1 overdue guest owing nothing
observed: The banner says "0 misafir bakiyeyle ayrılıyor" (0 guests leaving with a balance), and the table below shows the empty state "Bugün çıkış yok / Bu tesiste bugün ayrılması beklenen bir konaklama bulunmuyor" (No departures today / nobody is due to leave). suggested_fix: When a filter is active and has no rows, use a filter-specific empty state ("Nobody leaving today owes anything. N others are leaving."), and keep the Show all link in it.

where: Departures row vs check-out dialog, any guest with uncharged nights
observed: The row's Balance column renders balanceMinor only. The dialog computes due = balanceMinor + pendingMinor and adds a "Charged at check-out" line and "Balance after check-out" (ADR 0038). So a row can read TRY 0.00 (and not red) while the dialog shows an amount owing and demands a typed reason before it will confirm. The "owing" filter is typed on balanceMinor and overdue only (inDepartureFilter), so it has the same blind spot; I did not check how Today computes its own owing figure. On staging the booking is unpriced, so I could not see the mismatch.
expected: The list shows the same number the dialog is going to ask about, so the rush agent is not surprised at the confirm step.
suggested_fix: Show balance plus pending on the row, with a small "includes N nights charged at check-out" note, and use the same figure in the owing filter.
evidence: No screenshot possible. Code: columns.tsx Balance cell, check-out-dialog.tsx due.

where: Check-out dialog and Change departure dialog, overdue guest
observed: The row says "Overdue since Oct 1, 2026" (a date, not "10 days"). The check-out dialog shows only "Planned departure Oct 1, 2026" and does not say the guest is overdue, nor that the departure will be recorded as today (CO-S1-02). Change departure never mentions overdue; its date picker greys out all past dates, so an overdue guest who is staying can only be moved to tomorrow or later, and the dialog does not explain what the nights since Oct 1 will cost (unknown).
expected: "10 days overdue" on the row; the dialog says "Overdue: leaving today instead of Oct 1" so the agent knows what gets recorded.
suggested_fix: Badge text "10 days overdue (since Oct 1)". One line in the dialog for the overdue case. Ask the billing owner what an overdue extension charges and say it.

where: Check-out dialog and what follows, Front Desk

Per the roadmap a check-out marks the room dirty (migration a_check_out_makes_the_room_dirty) and the room is not ready to let until housekeeping cleans it. Arrivals shows a "Not ready" readiness badge and warns before check-in; Departures neither tells the agent the room is now dirty nor tells housekeeping anything visible on the page. expected: "Room 102 will be marked dirty and housekeeping will see it" before the click, and a confirmation after it.
suggested_fix: Add that sentence to the dialog summary. After success show a toast with the guest, room and "Room 102 is dirty". Add a room-status chip to Left today rows.

where: Check-out dialog with a balance (not reproducible on staging)
observed: Per the code, when anything is owing the dialog forces a typed reason (3 to 2000 characters) and offers only "Open the Folio" (a normal link, same tab). Settling means leaving the dialog, paying on the Folio, coming back and re-opening it; dismissing the dialog also clears what was typed. The hint reads "The Folio stays open with X on it, and your reason is recorded. A payment is recorded on the Folio." The easy path is to type a reason and leave the Folio open, not to settle.
expected: The settle-then-check-out path is the fast one: pay from the dialog, or return to the same dialog afterwards.
suggested_fix: Link to the Folio with a return to Departures. Add a "Record payment" step in the dialog (needs the Folio payment component). Consider a distinct, plainer first line: "Guest owes X. Collect payment first, or leave it open with a reason."

observed: (a) The page itself has no filter for owing or overdue: those narrowings exist only as ?show= links built from Today, and the filter strip only appears when one is applied. (b) Sort is by column header; the default order is planned departure only. (c) Page size is 10 (verified), so 15 departures span two pages. (d) Every check-out is its own dialog: open, review, confirm, repeated per row; no multi-select. (e) The list polls every 30 s, so a colleague's check-out removes your row (the code comment says so); I could not watch it happen.
expected: Two chips at the top, "Owing" and "Overdue", and a page size big enough that a rush fits on one screen.
suggested_fix: Add "Owing" and "Overdue" chips that set ?show=; default page size 25; keep the dialog per row for now and let Enter on the focused Confirm repeat quickly.
evidence: 01-due-desktop.png (Per page 10), 15-search-no-match.png (search works); polling and bulk inferred

observed: Both see the list (name, reservation, room, leaves, balance) but no Check out button and no explanation: the action column is just a "..." menu with Open folio and Show on the room map. Change departure and Move Guest are also absent. Housekeeping also sees each guest's balance; I could not tell whether that is intended (unknown), FD-S7-05 says readers see the rows.
expected: A short note ("You can view departures; check-out needs the front desk role") or a disabled button with a reason.
suggested_fix: Disabled Check out with a tooltip naming the permission, or a one-line note above the table.

observed: There is no view of "who owes money". The list has search and column sorting only. The "open folios" filter exists (?show=open) but is reachable only from a Today card; it means status open, not balance above zero. Default order is open first, then unit name, not balance or recency. The list query has no limit, so closed folios stay in the same list forever and all are loaded into one client table (read from module.ts: no limit).
expected: One click to "folios with a balance", largest first, and a way to hide closed ones.

observed: A folio is identified only by guest name and unit. No reservation reference, no stay dates, no check-out date, no charges / payments totals; only a "Lines" count, which means nothing to a clerk. Departures shows the same guest as R96J74P, overdue since Oct 1; Finance shows neither. No link from the folio to the reservation or Departures row.
expected: Explain a bill to a guest: whose stay, which nights, how much charged, how much paid, how much left.
suggested_fix: Add reference + stay dates to the list row and folio header; show Charged / Paid / Balance; replace "Lines" with last activity; link to the reservation.

where: folio view, Add a charge; Finance; open folio
observed: I typed a valid description and the amount 1,250.00 and pressed Post (the code returns "invalid" before any write, and the folio still showed no lines afterwards). The message was "An amount must be a positive number with no more decimal places than the currency allows." and both fields were emptied, so the clerk retypes everything. Thousands separators are not accepted by design (toMinorUnits allows digits plus one separator). In Turkish, 1.250,00 is the normal way to write 1,250 lira and is rejected the same way. I did not test Turkish.
expected: Keep what was typed, point at the amount, and say what is wrong ("remove the thousands separator" or, better, accept it).
suggested_fix: Keep field values after an "invalid" outcome (return them from the action state); accept locale grouping separators or say so in the message.
evidence: 13; reproduced Y (once; the second run was not repeated to avoid more submits)
basis: EN behaviour verified; TR behaviour inferred from lib/amount.ts

where: folio view: Post charge, Post payment, Reverse, Close folio; Finance / Owner; open folio
observed: Each is a plain form submit: no confirmation, no summary ("Record TRY 450.00 cash on ahmed, room 102?"), no undo. Reverse takes a reason inline and fires on Enter or click. Close folio does not state the balance it will close on, though closing is not settling (FO-S5-01). I did not press any of them.
expected: A money action names its consequence before the click, at least for payment, reversal and close-with-balance.
suggested_fix: Confirm dialog on Post payment, Reverse and Close (when balance is not zero), stating guest, amount, method and that the original line stays.
evidence: code only (folio-panel.tsx ChargeForm, PaymentForm, ReverseAction, CloseAction); not reproduced by design

where: folio view, Record payment; Finance, Front Desk, Owner
observed: Payment method is pre-selected to "Credit card" (defaultValue="card"), so a clerk who skips the field records cash as card. The amount is not prefilled with the balance, although folio-payments row FP-S1-15 (approved) says it is, and FP-S1-14 describes a "dialog/drawer" where the UI has two inline forms. The code has no overpayment check (only "greater than zero"), so TRY 5,000 can be recorded on a TRY 450 folio. There is no payment reference or receipt number field. Description is required free text.
expected: The payment form starts from the common case (balance due) with no hidden default for method, and refuses or confirms an amount above the balance.
suggested_fix: Prefill amount; make method a required choice; warn on amount above balance; add an optional reference.
basis: method default and missing prefill verified in UI/code; overpayment inferred (no check found in server/finance.ts; the module/DB may still refuse, I did not read it)

where: folio view with lines; reversal wording
observed: Reversal presentation could not be seen (no lines on staging). From code: the original line is struck through with the word "reversed", and the reversal is a second, negative line. For ordinary charges the reversal's description is the typed reason, with no "Reversal of ..." label and no link back to the original. The idea that history is never deleted is said only on a closed folio ("Its lines stay exactly as they are"). A clerk reversing a charge on an open folio is not told the original stays.
expected: Reading a bill with a reversed charge, a guest can tell what was charged, what was taken off and why.
suggested_fix: Label reversal lines ("Reversal: <reason>") next to the line they cancel; one sentence under the lines table about corrections.

observed: Housekeeping is not denied. Finance is in their rail; they see the folio list with the Balance column and open a folio with every line, read-only (no forms). Front Desk sees the folio, a Record payment form, and no Add a charge form. No explanation is given to either. The folio docs list this as undecided (FO-S7-02), but the Today docs say no balance goes to anybody without finance.manage_folio.
expected: Either a decision that housekeeping may read money (stated), or a denial that says "needs finance access".

where: folio view / list; Finance; in-house, overdue guest
observed: Folio "ahmed" shows 0 lines and TRY 0.00 while the Departures row says "Overdue since Oct 1, 2026", and Analytics says "0 of 31 days closed" with days 1-11 "Open day, Not yet charged". suggested_fix: On an open folio with no room-night lines, show "No nights charged yet: charged when the day is closed" with the last closed day; flag unpriced stays on the list.

observed: The sort buttons are announced as "Guest, Next" and "Balance, Next" and the sort menu text is "Next" / "Previous" / "Clear filter": useSortLabels maps sortAscending to table.next and sortDescending to table.previous. Shared kit, so it affects every list.

expected: On a phone, guest and balance are visible without scrolling.

observed: Money reads ₺0,00 in Turkish but TRY 0.00 in English and ‏0.00 TRY in Arabic, and the form label says "(TRY)" in all three. Turkish "Record payment" is "Ödeme al" (take payment), which suggests the system collects the money; the English means recording it. "Post" is "İşle" in Turkish (to process) and "قيد" in Arabic. The "Folio lines" table caption sits below the table. The Back button does go to the Finance list (verified, ADR 0035 met).

observed: "Posted" times are formatted in a client component with no timeZone option, so they show in the browser's time zone, not the Property's (Europe/Istanbul). Room-night dates are the only ones pinned to UTC. A clerk travelling or a server render in UTC could show a charge on the wrong business day. A line's business date is a deferred row (FO-DEF-08).
expected: Times and days in the Property's time zone.
suggested_fix: Pass the Property time zone to formatDate.

observed: No way to assign a request to a person or department. There is no Assignee column and no assign control. The server action assignServiceRequest and the data field assignedToName exist, and the message keys assignee / unassigned exist, but nothing renders or calls them (grep: no consumer outside server/guest-services.ts). Use case use-case.mmd and edge case GX-S1-13 (approved) both say staff can assign.
expected: See who owns each request; pick a person (or department) from the row; filter "unassigned".

where: Row action "Reopen" on a Cancelled request, Front Desk/Manager
observed: Reopen always sends in_progress. The database trigger rejects that for cancelled rows ("a cancelled request can only be reopened to new"), and the check (status='cancelled') = (cancel_reason is not null) also fails because the UI does not clear the reason. The server action catches the error and returns "refused", which the UI ignores. So Reopen on a cancelled request does nothing and says nothing. Also states.mmd says cancelled reopens to New.
expected: Request returns to New, cancel reason cleared, and I see it move to Open.
suggested_fix: Send new with cancelReason: null for cancelled; show the result.

where: All row actions (Start working, Resolve, Cancel, Reopen), all roles
observed: Results are never read: await updateServiceRequestStatus(...) is called and its {status} thrown away; the Resolve and Cancel dialogs close afterwards regardless of the outcome. There is no toast, success or error message anywhere on the page. A refusal (no permission, database rule, network) is indistinguishable from success until the list refreshes. Also the Cancel button enables for 1 or 2 characters but the database requires 3-200, so a short reason silently fails.
expected: A confirmation ("Request #12 resolved") or an error saying why it did not work; dialog stays open on failure with the text kept.
suggested_fix: Use the returned outcome; show toast or FormError; keep dialog open on refusal; validate the 3-character minimum client side; use useActionState as the create dialog does. Per the global observability rule, the console.error in the server action is the only record of failure.

where: Open tab with many requests, Front Desk
observed: No age and no priority ordering. The only time shown is "Reported" as a fixed "Oct 11, 14:05". The query sorts status asc, createdAt desc, which is alphabetical status: "in_progress" sorts before "new", so a brand-new request sits below things already being worked on, and an Urgent one is not lifted. There is no "waiting 3h" and no overdue highlight. The only urgency signal is a badge in one of nine columns, and the Urgent stat tile only counts (it is not a filter).
expected: Open tab sorted urgent first, then oldest first, with "waiting 2h 10m" visible, amber/red after a threshold.
suggested_fix: Sort client or server side by priority then reportedAt asc; show relative age; make the Urgent tile click-filter.

observed: Housekeeping sees the same page as Front Desk, including "New Request", with no explanation of what they may do. Shipped Housekeeping role may create but not manage requests (migration lines 106-120), yet the row actions (Start working, Resolve, Cancel) are drawn for every role with no permission check, so for Housekeeping they would be buttons that fail silently (see GX-03). Maintenance, by contrast, shows a "read only" notice (board.mayManage). The queue also shows every category to every role, with no "my department" filter.
expected: Housekeeping sees requests for their category first, and buttons they cannot use are hidden or explained.
suggested_fix: Pass mayManage to the table; hide or disable actions with a reason; add category filter and default it by role.
evidence: Page seen as Housekeeping (same zero-data layout, "New Request" present); buttons not seen
basis: verified (same page, New Request shown) + inferred (actions)

Neither names the request or when the room is expected back, so the desk cannot answer a guest asking "when?" without opening Rooms. No room was out of order on staging.
expected: The same reference and back date everywhere the room is shown as unavailable.
suggested_fix: Pass the hold reference and expected-back date to the badge in Arrivals and the calendar.

observed: The dialog says "You pass the link on yourself" but the code shows a bare 43-character token in a text box (invite-dialog.tsx renders outcome.token), not a URL. The only consumer of the token is the module function accept(); nothing in apps/ calls it (grep) and edge-cases.csv SP-S1-32 says "no route is wired". The sign-in page has no set-password or forgot-password link. The invited user row exists and the membership is already active, so the person is on the roster as "Awaiting a password" with no way to get one.
expected: Invite, copy a working link, the receptionist opens it, sets a password and signs in on Monday.
suggested_fix: Build the accept-invitation page and show a full URL; until then, say on the dialog that sign-in for new staff is not available. Email delivery (blueprint 5.12) is a separate prerequisite.
evidence: 03; sign-in screenshot not taken (page text read via snapshot). Not submitted.
