where: People tab, row "..." menu, Owner and Manager
observed: "Revoke" is the only item in the row menu and runs on one press: MembershipActions.run() calls revokeStaffMember directly with no dialog. The copy never says that every session of that person ends at once (SP-S1-11), that nothing is deleted, that the row stays as "Revoked", that "Undo" works only for 24 hours (SP-S1-22), or what happens to their open work. A refusal appears only after the press, in red next to the menu. Owner and Manager can also revoke themselves from their own row.
expected: A confirmation naming the person, "signed out everywhere now", "you can undo for 24 hours", and for self-revoke a warning like the role-change one.
suggested_fix: Reuse the role-change confirmation pattern (confirm-role-change.tsx) for revoke and undo; show the undo deadline on the revoked row.
basis: inferred from roster-table.tsx. Deliberately not pressed.

observed: Role defaults to "Finance" (first item alphabetically: code picks roles[0]), the Properties field is empty and reads "No Property yet", and nothing warns that an invitee with no Property reaches nothing. No role description is shown anywhere in the picker. There is no way to choose "every Property" (code never sends a scope).
expected: No default role (force a choice), or the least-privileged role; a visible warning when no Property is chosen; one line describing the chosen role.
suggested_fix: Start with an empty role field; show "Reaches no Property yet" in amber; add a one-line role description under the picker.
basis: verified default and placeholder; inferred consequence of an empty Property.

where: "What each role can do" tab and Invite, Manager
observed: Manager has a tick on every one of the 31 permissions, identical to Owner. The only difference between them is reach (Owner = every Property). As Manager, the invite role list offers "Owner", so a Manager can create an Owner-equivalent colleague. The screen never explains what an Owner has that a Manager lacks. Manager sees the Owner row locked with "Their role or reach is above yours.", which is the only hint, and it is about reach, not role.
expected: A visible difference, or a plain sentence: "Owner and Manager can do the same things; Owner reaches every Property."
suggested_fix: Product decision first: if Manager should not see payroll, ledger or hand out Owner, remove those ticks. Then add a role description line under each column.
basis: verified grid and invite options. Whether the equality is intended is unknown.

where: "What each role can do" tab, Owner, once an Organization has its own role
observed: For an Organization-authored role every box is a live toggle that saves immediately (toggle() calls editRole), and the header "Retire" is a one-press menu item. Editing a role ends the sessions of everyone holding it (use-case.mmd: EDITROLE includes ENDSESS). The only warning is the "held by N" count in the column header; there is no confirmation and a refusal shows only as a line at the foot of the grid. Staging has no authored roles, so this was not seen.
expected: A confirmation: "4 people hold this role; saving signs them out."
suggested_fix: Batch ticks behind a "Save changes" button with a count of affected people.
evidence: none (no authored role to look at)

where: "What each role can do" tab, Owner; cross-screen
observed: To answer "who can see money?" I had to read 31 flat rows. Money-related rows are scattered (Folio, charge, payment, ledger, data exports, rates, payroll) and there are no section headings. There is no "who holds this?" view per permission and no per-person effective-access view. Cross-screen: Analytics revenue figures are gated by the permission shown here as "Open and close a Folio" (handover doc), and Front Desk holds it. Signed in as Front Desk, Analytics shows the Revenue and "Money collected" cards (all 0.00 on this data).
expected: Grouped rows (Front desk, Money, Staff, Setup...) and a "Money" shortcut or highlight; a person's name in the row for each role.
suggested_fix: Group the catalogue; add a "who can see money" filter; name the revenue gate in plain words.
basis: verified flat grid and the Front Desk revenue cards; inferred that the gate is the Folio permission.

observed: The link is shown once and "never again". If the owner closes the dialog before copying it, nothing re-issues it: inviting an existing member returns "That person already has a membership" (invite() inserts with on conflict do nothing). The "Awaiting a password" badge offers no action. After the 24-hour undo window a revoked person also appears to hit that same refusal, although SP-S1-15/16 describe a re-invite path; I did not run it.
expected: A "New link" action on any "Awaiting a password" row, and a way to bring a revoked person back.
suggested_fix: Add "Resend / new link" and "Re-add" row actions.
basis: inferred; the revoked-person re-add is unknown.

where: People tab, 375 px and 768 px, Owner
observed: The table is about 728 px wide inside a card of 341 px at 375 and roughly 460 px at 768 (the sidebar stays open at 768). Properties, Status and the "..." Actions menu sit off-screen to the right with no scroll hint, so on a phone you can see a role picker but not Revoke. No page-level horizontal scroll.
expected: Rows that stack on narrow widths, or at least a visible scroll cue.
suggested_fix: Card layout below 768 px: email, role, status on one line, actions at the end.

observed: People are identified by email only (avatar initials are derived from it); there is no name column, no search, no filter by role or Property, no sort, and no pagination in the code (roster.map). Revoked people stay in the list permanently. With 30 staff the owner scrolls and reads addresses.
expected: Search box, role filter, "show revoked" toggle, a display name.
suggested_fix: Add search and a revoked filter; a name field is a schema decision (code comment says so).
basis: verified (emails, no search box at 5 rows); inferred (no pagination, revoked stay).

observed: The dialog says "housekeeping... will go from Housekeeping to Manager. Every session they hold will end" and nothing about what they gain or lose. Going from Housekeeping to Manager would give them payroll and ledger access. Good: Cancel has focus, the title is a question, self-demotion and last-administrator cases have their own text (inferred).
expected: A short "gains: payroll, ledger... / loses: ..." line.
suggested_fix: Compute the permission difference and list the money and staff items.
basis: verified dialog; cancelled with Escape, role unchanged afterwards (re-read the roster).

where: Revoke and role change, last administrator
observed: The last-administrator rule is predicted before the confirm for a role change (leavesNoAdministrator) but not for Revoke, where it is refused after the press with "An Organization must keep somebody who can add staff." That text does not say what to do (make another Owner first). Other failures are only "That was refused."
expected: The same pre-check on revoke, and a next step in the message.
suggested_fix: Call leavesNoAdministrator for revoke; reword to "Make another Owner first."

where: All locales, row menu and grid
observed: English "Revoke" is jargon; Turkish "Kaldır" and Arabic "إلغاء العضوية" read as "remove / cancel membership", so the three locales do not say the same thing. Role "Retire" is "Emekliye ayır" (retire as in pension) in Turkish and "إحالة إلى التقاعد" in Arabic; the English "Retire" itself does not say the role is switched off. Permission labels mix forms ("Reading the audit log", "Take a booking") and use product terms ("Folio", "Guests", "Close the day") with no explanation.
expected: Plain, consistent verbs: "Remove access", "Switch off role".
suggested_fix: One wording pass across the three catalogues.
basis: verified grid labels; inferred menu labels from messages.ts.

where: "What each role can do" tab, all roles
observed: Shipped-role boxes are disabled checkboxes, so the ticks are pale grey on white; at a glance the grid reads as empty. There is also no "Define a role" starting point such as "copy Front desk": the dialog is 31 unticked, ungrouped boxes in a scrolling modal.
expected: Clearly readable ticks for read-only boxes; copy-from for a new role.
suggested_fix: Use a solid tick icon for read-only state; add "Start from..." to the dialog.

observed: Front Desk is not denied. They see the whole roster (every colleague's email, role and Property) and the permission grid, read-only, with "You can see the team. An Owner or Manager can change it." That is the documented design ("any Staff Member reads the roster"), so it is clear and calm, but the sentence hard-codes two role names, and a custom role holding "Administer staff" would also qualify.
expected: Decide deliberately whether a receptionist or housekeeper should see colleagues' emails.
suggested_fix: Either keep, or say "People who manage staff can change it".

observed: Cards are rendered in the order the read returns them: name, then id (derive.ts, portfolio-view.tsx, PF-S1-27). No sort control, no rank, no “behind” marker. Each card leads with a raw count (“10 / 20”); the percentage is a 12px caption and the bar is 6px high. Summary tiles say nothing about the spread between Properties.
expected: To spot the Property that is behind in under five seconds: sort by occupancy share, money owed, open maintenance or arrivals still to come, and the share shown as the large figure.
suggested_fix: Add a sort control (default stays name), make the share the headline figure with the count beneath, and optionally mark the lowest and highest in each metric. Needs a design decision on what “behind” means; do not invent targets.

where: /portfolio, any viewer where money is hidden at some Properties but not others
observed: The Money owed summary tile is built without a coverage prop (summary-stats.tsx, second SummaryCard). balancesOf() in server/portfolio.ts skips null balances, so a Property with billing off drops out of the sum silently. The occupancy and maintenance tiles do print “Counted at x of y Properties”; the money tile does not. The page-level amber notice fires only when every entitled Property hides money (moneyHidden).
expected: The same guard as the other two tiles. derive.ts states the rule itself: “a sum over fewer Properties than are listed, shown without that, would be an understatement that reads as a fact.”
suggested_fix: Compute money coverage (Properties with a non-null balance vs listed) per currency or overall and pass it to the tile.

observed: An unknown or no-longer-reached Property id (a stale bookmark, a Property unassigned since) shows the heading “This module is not in your Subscription” and “It appears here once your Organization subscribes to it and the Property has it enabled.” The URL is left unchanged, the Property button reads “Properties” (the switcher still lists the real one), and every rail link and the back button carry the bogus id forward (verified in the accessibility snapshot).
expected: A message that says the Property in the link is not available to me and offers my real Property. The edge-case rows PF-S2-04 and PF-S2-15 call this “the not-available state” and the page reuses the Subscription copy for it.
suggested_fix: Give the page its own not-available copy, or drop an unreached ?property= and fall back to the viewer’s first Property as Today does. The Subscription wording is right only when no reached Property has Analytics.
evidence: 04-owner-forged-property.png; reproduced Y (twice, in two page loads)

observed: The only action on a card is “Open <Property>”, a plain link to Today at that Property (open-property.tsx). The figures are text, not links: “Arrivals still to come: 5”, “Open maintenance: 7” and “Money owed” cannot be clicked to the list behind them.
expected: When a figure looks wrong I click it and land on that list for that Property (arrivals, maintenance, finance).
suggested_fix: Make each figure a link to its destination with ?property= set, using the same remember-then-full-load behaviour. Keep “Open” for Today. Note a destination may be switched off at that Property; Today already handles that fallback.

observed: The page is one server read with no refresh control and no polling (it is not a live screen). The stamp reads “Figures as of {time}” with a time only, in the working Property’s zone (page.tsx, formatTime). Each card shows its own business date, so a tab left open overnight shows yesterday’s figures with a plausible time-of-day and no date.
expected: A date with the time, and a way to refresh without reloading the browser. This matters for an owner who keeps the tab open all day.
suggested_fix: Show date and time in the stamp, add a refresh button (router refresh), and say which time zone the time is in when the Properties differ.

observed: Cards are 3 across at xl, 2 across at md, one column below (portfolio-view.tsx); the loading skeleton gives a card a height of 288px. Twelve cards is about four rows plus the summary row, so more than one screen on a 900px-high laptop and the summary scrolls away. No search, filter or compact (table) mode. Above 200 reached Properties the whole page is replaced by “Too many Properties to compare” with no way to narrow the set (PF-S1-28, deliberate).
expected: With a dozen Properties, a dense table or a compact card that fits all twelve in one screen, and a filter to get under the ceiling.
suggested_fix: Offer a compact table view with sortable columns (pairs with PORTFOLIO-01). For the ceiling, a filter by region/group once Properties have one; today there is nothing to filter by.
evidence: Code and loading skeleton only; card height is from the skeleton, not measured

where: /portfolio, all roles; one-Property view verified, populated copy from messages.ts
observed: (a) The one-Property message says “You reach one Property”. “Reach” is system language; an Owner means “you have one Property”. It also does not say who can add or assign another. (b) The summary tile is called “Occupancy across Properties” but each card labels the same measure “Units in use”. (c) “Folio” is capitalised mid-sentence in “Open Folio balances”; that is the product vocabulary, but this persona may call it a bill or an account.
expected: One name per measure across the tile and the cards; plain wording for the owner.
suggested_fix: Use “Occupancy” on both, reword to “You have one Property: …”, and name who can add a Property (if that is a built feature).

where: /en/reservations, Front Desk, one in-house overdue guest
observed: ahmed is in house in Room 102 and overdue (arrived Sep 29, due out Oct 1; Room calendar drawer says "Overdue: they were due to leave on Oct 1, 2026"). Reservations shows 1 row (a different guest) and the tab "In house" shows 0. The new-booking Unit list marks 102 "Someone is staying then".
expected: Every guest who is physically in house is on the list under "In house", especially an overdue one, who is the one who needs an extend or a check-out.
suggested_fix: Make the list query keep checked-in / in-house bookings whatever their end date. The filter keeps a booking when ends_on >= today or status is requested/confirmed, so a checked-in booking with a past end date drops out (listReservations in packages/ranza/reservations/src/module.ts).
evidence: 29, 01, 07. Reproduced Y (repeated list read after reload)

where: /en/reservations, Front Desk, 1200 px window, sidebar open, 1 row
observed: The table is 1048 px wide inside a 896 px area. On load the Status column is the last visible one; Check in and the "..." menu are off the right edge until you scroll the table sideways. Opening the row menu scrolls the table and pushes the Guest column out of view. At 1440 px it fits. A longer email or name would widen it further (column widths are content-driven).
expected: The row action is always visible at the laptop widths a desk actually uses (1280-1366).
suggested_fix: Pin the Action column at the trailing edge (sticky), or default the sidebar to collapsed under ~1400 px, or drop the Price/Status columns into the Columns menu below a width.

observed: 768 px: the sidebar stays open, the page itself scrolls sideways (document 829 px), the status tabs are clipped ("Upcon"), the breadcrumb truncates to "W( > F..", and Unit/Price/Status/Action are off-screen. 375 px (emulated mobile): the layout viewport grows to 573 px, the tab strip and table are cut off, and the New reservation dialog is wider than the screen so the close button and the Create button are off-screen.
expected: A card-style row on a phone with the status and the primary action visible, and a dialog that fits the screen.
suggested_fix: Under ~768 px render each booking as a stacked card (guest, dates, unit, status, action); make the dialog max-w-[calc(100vw-2rem)]; collapse the sidebar by default under 1024 px.
basis: verified in emulation. A real phone may differ in how the viewport expands, so treat the exact 573 px as emulator-specific.

observed: Works: reference (any case, partial), guest name (partial), unit, unit type, status word, "oct 11", "11 oct", "2026-10-11", phone typed as one digit run. Fails (0 results): the same phone typed with spaces or with +90, a partial phone with a space, "11.10.2026", "11/10" (the formats a Turkish desk types), two words from different fields ("guest-name email-domain"), and a one-letter typo in the name.
expected: Feature doc RG-S4-16: "the digits find the booking though the number was written with spaces". A phone number read out loud is typed in whatever format the caller says it.
suggested_fix: Normalise the typed query the same way the stored phone is (strip spaces, +, leading 0/90), parse dd.mm.yyyy and dd/mm, and match every word of a multi-word query against the row instead of the whole string against one field.
evidence: 12. Y (ran all queries in one session, results consistent)
basis: verified. The doc contradiction is inferred from RG-S4-16 (status "proposed").

observed: There is no guest search. Typing the exact name of an existing guest shows nothing. The only de-duplication is an exact email match ("An address already on file books that same Guest again"). A returning guest who phones in with a name and number but no email becomes a second guest record, silently.
expected: While typing the name or phone, a suggestion "Existing guest: use this one?" so a repeat guest is reused.
suggested_fix: Add a lookup on name and phone as they are typed, shown as a suggestion list, never an automatic merge (blueprint 18.7 forbids that). The duplicate-review screen is deferred (RG-DEF-05), so a lookup at booking time is the cheap prevention.
evidence: Typed an existing guest's name, no listbox appeared (checked the dialog DOM). Y
basis: verified. The matching rule is by design: RG-S1-18 (approved) says exact email only.

where: New reservation dialog and Change booking, Front Desk, no rate set for the unit type
observed: After choosing a unit the dialog shows a small grey box: "No price is set for Room here, so this booking is taken without one and its nights are not charged." Nothing stops or colours it as a warning. On staging no unit type has a price, so every booking taken today would be uncharged. Detail sheet then shows Price "No price" and "1 night: --". The priced path (per-night rate and stay total) exists in code but I could not see it.
expected: A visible warning (amber, with an icon) when the booking will not earn revenue, and for a desk without rate permission a way to tell the manager.
suggested_fix: Style the unpriced notice as a warning and repeat it in the confirmation row; consider a Property-level "bookings need a price" setting.
basis: verified (notice), inferred (revenue consequence, RT-S3-01 charges nights at the close; priced state not seen)

where: New reservation dialog, invalid input, Front Desk
observed: (a) Empty submit: the browser's own bubble "Please fill out this field." (in the browser's language, not the product's) pops over the product's inline message "Enter the Guest's name." and hides it; same for a bad email, where the product's line "Enter a valid email address, such as name@example.com, or leave it empty." is partly covered. (b) With no Unit and no dates only the name/Unit get inline errors; Stay dates shows no error, only the grey hint. (c) Telephone accepts "abc".
expected: One message per problem, in the product's language, on every invalid field including dates; a phone field that rejects letters (this also feeds search, RES-04).
suggested_fix: Add noValidate on the form and rely on the inline messages, add the missing dates message, validate phone characters.
basis: verified (RG-S4-19 expects several problems at once; only two of three were shown)

observed: Pressing Escape on a half-filled booking closes the dialog with no warning and the next open is blank (typed name, email, phone lost). Clicking outside was not tested.
expected: A phone call gets interrupted; the form either keeps its draft or asks "Discard this booking?".
suggested_fix: Keep the draft in state until Create/Cancel, or confirm the discard when the form is dirty.
evidence: Escape then reopen, guest field empty (DOM check). Y

where: Row menu → Mark as no-show, Front Desk, a Confirmed booking arriving today
observed: The menu offers it as soon as the arrival day starts. The dialog states "The Guest did not come. The nights are freed, and this cannot be taken back." as a fact, takes no reason, and the red button commits in one click. Focus starts on "Keep the booking", which is the right safe default.
expected: On the arrival day before the Property's cutoff, the guest may simply be late; the wording should not assert they did not come, or the action should wait for the cutoff / ask for a reason.
suggested_fix: Offer no-show only after the expected arrival time or cutoff, or add a required one-line reason like Cancel has.
basis: verified (dialog), inferred (the SQL mayMarkNoShow has only starts_on <= today)

where: Row menu → Cancel booking, Front Desk
observed: Reason is a required free-text box (minimum 3 characters, enforced by the browser's own tooltip "Please fill out this field."). No placeholder, no common reasons to pick. The dialog says "A cancellation cannot be taken back" but does not say what happens to a price or fee (none exists yet) or that rebooking means a fresh booking with a new reference.
expected: 40 bookings a day means many cancellations; a quick pick ("Guest cancelled", "Duplicate", "Wrong dates", "Other...") plus the free text.
suggested_fix: Preset reasons as chips that fill the box; name "to restore it you must make a new booking".
evidence: 17, 18. Stopped before submit (form was invalid, so the click could not submit).

where: New reservation dialog, Front Desk, phone-in flow
observed: Field order is Guest, Email, Phone, Unit, Stay type, Dates. A caller asks "do you have a room for the 20th to the 22nd?", but availability only appears after dates are chosen, and the Unit you picked first can then turn into "taken for the nights you chose". No count of nights or stay total is shown while no price exists. The date picker covers the dialog title while open.
expected: Dates first, then only the free Units (with prices), then the guest.
suggested_fix: Put Stay dates before Unit, and show "N nights" next to the dates always.

observed: (a) Unit appears twice: as a read-only block "Unit 201" near the top and again as the editable "Unit" field. (b) Guest and Reservation are large read-only blocks that push the real fields down (Note box clipped at 900 px height until scrolled). (e) Unit list order is 201, 101, 102 (not sorted). (f) Cancel button reads "Keep as it was".
expected: One compact header (guest, reference), the change summarised ("Oct 11 - Oct 13, 2 nights, no price change"), conflict names the guest and dates.
suggested_fix: Remove the duplicate Unit block, add a change summary line, sort Units.

where: Booking detail side sheet, Front Desk
observed: Clicking a row opens a sheet that shows dates, unit, contact and price, but its only action is "Check in". Change booking, Mark as no-show and Cancel exist only in the row's "..." menu. After reading a booking you close the sheet and find the menu. The subtitle "Guest · Reservation details" shows the stay type as "Guest", which reads like a label for the person. Billing card shows "1 night" over a bare dash.
expected: From the detail view, the same actions as the row.
suggested_fix: Add the row menu actions to the sheet footer; hide or fill the empty billing line.

observed: Neither role is denied. Both get the full page: the same list with each guest's email and phone and the Price column, no New reservation button, no row actions, and no sentence saying the page is read-only. The sidebar for Housekeeping shows every module (Finance, People, HR, Analytics, Configuration). The empty "Action" column header remains. The brief expected the page to be absent or denied.
expected: A housekeeper has no need for guest phone numbers and emails; if the view is intentional it should say "View only".
suggested_fix: Owner decision: either gate the page (or the contact column) by permission, or mask contact details for non-front-desk roles, and show a "View only" note.
basis: verified. Intent unknown: RG-S3-02 (approved) says each row carries the guest's email for "the viewer", with no role split.

observed: Turkish and Arabic are complete and RTL mirrors correctly (date arrow, columns, buttons). Gaps: the dialog's close control text reads "Close" in English in both (innerText of the dialog); in Turkish the page subtitle repeats the title ("Rezervasyonlar — Demo Otel Istanbul") where English says "Bookings at ...". expected: No English left in tr/ar; one term per concept.
suggested_fix: Translate the close label; align subtitle; pick one Arabic term.

observed: "Guest" is both the person field and the Stay type value (Stay type: Guest). "Unit" is the field name but values are "Room" and "Suite" and the notice says "No price is set for Room". Availability words differ between dialogs: New says "Someone is staying then" / "Booked for these nights" (disabled), Change says "Somebody is staying" / "Free" (selectable).
expected: One vocabulary.

observed: Not observable with one row. The list query has no LIMIT; every open booking plus everything ending today or later is sent to the browser and searched, sorted and paged client-side (page size 10 by default). Sort is by start date only.
expected: Search stays instant with a few hundred rows.
suggested_fix: Measure with a seeded 500-row Property before rollout; server-side search if it is slow.

observed: First screen is page title, a duplicate heading, a 3-line description, date controls, three filters, search, two checkboxes and a 4-row legend. The grid starts about 760 px down, partly under the bottom nav. The room column is 11rem, so only about two days are visible beside it.
expected: The grid is the first thing I see; filters and legend tuck away; more than two days show.
suggested_fix: On narrow screens: collapse filters and legend behind one button, drop the second heading and the description, shrink the room column to about 4rem.

where: 30-day view, English and Turkish, Front Desk
observed: Day headers are one letter plus a number: T F S S M T W T F S S M T. Thursday and Tuesday are both T, Saturday and Sunday both S. Turkish is P C C P (Pazartesi and Pazar are both P; Cuma and Cumartesi both C). The month change has no marker: the header reads S31 then S1 with no label.
expected: I can tell which day and which month a column is without counting from the highlighted today column.
suggested_fix: Use a two-letter or short weekday at 30 days, with Sat/Sun columns tinted, and a month label (Nov) over the first day of each month.

where: 14 and 30 days, all roles; also Arabic
observed: A one-night booking cannot show its Guest: mahn… at 14 days, m at 30 days. After scrolling sideways a bar that started left of the pinned room column shows only a stub (ahn…). In Arabic the truncation cuts the front: …noor. The only way to read the name is the native tooltip delay or opening the drawer.
expected: I can tell who is in 201 without opening anything.
suggested_fix: Put the name beside or above a short bar, or show the name in a hover card with no delay; keep the label visible when the bar is partly under the sticky column.

where: Drawer of an overdue stay (102, ahmed), Front Desk, Housekeeping
observed: The bar runs to tonight, but the drawer says Arrived Sep 29, Leaves Oct 1, Booked Sep 27 to Oct 1, Nights 2, Balance TRY 0.00. The Guest is in the room 10 nights past the date shown, and nothing says nights since Oct 1 are not counted or not charged. where: Move booking dialog, Front Desk, first 1 to 2 seconds
